originalTitle: Nvidia’s $500 billion plan envelops Wall Street in its AI frenzy
simplifiedContent: Nvidia, a big technology company, has announced a huge plan worth $500 billion to help support the development of artificial intelligence (AI) technology. The plan involves working with big banks to provide loans to startups that are working on AI projects, especially those that need powerful computer chips. This is important because the demand for strong computing power is increasing rapidly, and Nvidia's plan aims to meet this demand. By doing this, Nvidia hopes to help build the necessary infrastructure for the tech industry to support AI growth. This plan is significant because it shows Nvidia's commitment to supporting the development of AI technology, which could have a big impact on the future of the tech industry.

originalTitle: How a $900 million bet on SpaceX turned 100x into $94 billion for Alphabet
simplifiedContent: Alphabet, the company that owns Google, invested $900 million in SpaceX a while back. That investment is now worth a staggering $94 billion, which is a huge return of 100 times the original amount. This means Alphabet now owns a very large portion of SpaceX, making it the largest shareholder. Other early investors, such as Fidelity Investments and Saudi Arabia's investment fund, also own significant parts of the company. This is significant because it shows how a large and successful investment can greatly increase in value over time.

originalTitle: Patanjali Foods Q1 Results: Gross profit rises 35% YoY to Rs 1,521 crore
simplifiedContent: Patanjali Foods, a company that makes and sells food products, just released its financial results for the first quarter of the year. The company did well, with its total sales (called revenue) increasing by 29.33% to ₹11,337 crore. The company's gross profit, which is the money it makes after subtracting the cost of making its products, also increased by 35.22%. This is good news for investors, as the company is making more money and is even paying out extra dividends to its shareholders. The strong results show that the company is performing well and executing its business plans effectively.

originalTitle: Patanjali Foods shares to be in focus on Monday as Q1 net profit jumps 86%; revenue hits record
simplifiedContent: Patanjali Foods, a company listed on the stock market, had a very good first quarter (April to June) with its profit increasing by 86% compared to the same time last year. The company made a profit of ₹335.73 crore and had its highest-ever revenue of ₹11,337.45 crore. This means the company performed better than expected, which might make its shares more attractive to investors. As a result, people might be interested in buying or selling Patanjali Foods shares on Monday, which could affect the company's stock price. The company has also announced that it will pay an interim dividend of 40% to its shareholders for this financial year.

originalTitle: Alphabet's $900 million SpaceX bet soars to $94 billion after rocket firm's IPO, filings show
simplifiedContent: Alphabet, the company that owns Google, invested $900 million in a company called SpaceX, which launches rockets into space. Recently, SpaceX had an Initial Public Offering (IPO), which is when a company starts selling its shares to the public. After the IPO, it was found that Alphabet's investment is now worth about $94 billion, which is a huge increase. This makes Alphabet the largest institutional owner of SpaceX, meaning they have the most shares of the company. This is significant because it shows that Alphabet's investment in SpaceX has been very successful and is now worth a lot more than they originally put in.

originalTitle: Sebi proposes overhaul of settlement rules to cut amounts, speed enforcement
simplifiedContent: The Indian stock market regulator, Sebi, wants to change the rules for settling cases where companies or people have broken the rules. They propose a new formula that could reduce the amount of money that needs to be paid to settle a case, making it closer to the final penalty. This change aims to speed up the process of resolving these cases. By doing this, Sebi hopes to resolve cases faster and make the process more efficient. This matters because it could help to quickly punish those who break the rules and make the stock market a fairer place.
